tasks.instruction: Read the text below. Choose the correct answer A, B or C for each question.
tasks.text:
THE BET

Filip said he could go a whole month without sugar. He announced it at lunch on the first of March, in front of everyone, which was his first mistake. His second was letting Ola set the terms.

'Nothing with sugar in it,' she said. 'Not sweets, not fizzy drinks, not biscuits, not that cereal you eat. And if you lose, you write the class newsletter for the rest of the year.'

'And if I win?'

'Then I write it.'

Nobody expected him to last a week. Filip is the person who keeps chocolate in his pencil case. But by the tenth of March he was still going, reading the back of every packet in the school shop and complaining loudly about how much sugar there is in bread.

The difficult part, he told me later, was not the sweets. It was that everything else suddenly tasted strange. Fruit seemed sweeter. Tea he had always drunk with two spoonfuls became undrinkable, then, after about two weeks, perfectly normal.

On the twenty-eighth his grandmother arrived with a cake she had made for his birthday. He ate two slices in front of the whole family and did not mention the bet to anybody.

He told Ola the truth the next morning. She looked at him for a long moment and then said she would write the newsletter anyway, because anyone who could refuse sugar for twenty-seven days and then admit to failing on the twenty-eighth had already won something.

items.stem: Why does the narrator call announcing the bet at lunch Filip's 'first mistake'?
options: A) He was not allowed to eat in the classroom.
B) Doing it publicly meant he could not quietly give up.
C) He forgot to agree what the prize would be.

items.stem: What did Filip find hardest about the month?
options: A) Giving up sweets and fizzy drinks.
B) Reading the labels on every packet.
C) The way familiar food began to taste different.

items.stem: What happened on the twenty-eighth of March?
options: A) He broke the bet at a family celebration.
B) He admitted to Ola that he had failed.
C) His grandmother reminded him about the bet.

items.stem: Why did Ola decide to write the newsletter herself?
options: A) She had lost the bet on a technicality.
B) She respected him for owning up.
C) She had promised his grandmother she would.

items.stem: What does 'had already won something' suggest?
options: A) Filip gained something other than the bet itself.
B) Filip had in fact won the bet.
C) Ola thought the terms had been unfair.

items.stem: Which word best describes the narrator's attitude to Filip?
